name: fact_picker
written: 2026-11-11 evening ET, before tools/fact_picker.py was run on any week (live or past)
why: operator 11/11: 'build the fact-sheet picker with the free data'. The headline-only picker (auto_picker) gives the agents no valuation, financials, performance, risk or technicals. Its 12-week replay showed no sign of skill at one month, and keeping only the names both agents picked did not help. This asks one new question: do the same two agents pick better for the next one to two months when each name comes with a fact sheet?
what_runs: tools/fact_picker.py run, Mondays 08:45 ET on the mini (com.jambi.fact-picker). No orders are placed. The auto_picker ledgers and their rules are not touched.
pool: symbols on the frozen list (docs/studies/pick_ledger_universe.txt) named in the past 7 days' headlines (the same headline pull as auto_picker), that have at least 252 daily bars and SEC revenue, net income and share-count facts filed before the run. If more than 100 qualify, the 100 named in the most headlines (ties alphabetical). A week with fewer than 20 names on the sheet records nothing. Dropped from the pool: foreign filers (20-F / 40-F; ADR share ratios are not in the data) and companies whose facts are not in US dollars.
fact_sheet: one line per name, all known before the run: prices through the prior close (Alpaca daily, adjusted); SEC XBRL company facts with a filing date before the run date. VALUATION: market value, price/earnings, price/sales, price/book (trailing twelve months). FINANCIALS: revenue growth vs the same period a year earlier, net margin, operating cash flow / net income, debt (liabilities) / equity. PERFORMANCE: 1, 3, 6, 12-month return and 3-month return minus SPY. RISK: 60-day annualized volatility, 1-year worst drawdown, 1-year beta. TECHNICALS: price vs 50- and 200-day average, 14-day RSI, distance below the 52-week high. Plus up to 2 of the week's headlines for the name. A figure that cannot be computed is shown as n/a, never guessed. The SEC tag for each figure is chosen from filings visible at the run date (on a tie, the larger value). The filed share count is scaled by raw close / split-adjusted close at its period end, so a later split does not make a name look cheap.
not_included: analyst price targets and earnings estimates: no free source. The agents are told not to supply them from memory.
ask: each agent (AGY and Grok, same models and no-tool settings as auto_picker) gets the same sheet and returns a 0-100 score for EVERY name: its expected return relative to the S&P 500 over the next one to two months.
combine: combined score = mean of the two agents' scores, over names both scored. If either agent returns fewer than half the names, nothing is recorded that week. PICKS = the 3 highest combined scores not picked in the past 92 days (ties alphabetical) -> ledger ~/pick_ledgers/facts. Shadow ledgers, same rules: AVOID = the 3 lowest combined scores -> ~/pick_ledgers/facts_avoid; RANDOM = 3 names drawn from the same pool, seeded by the date -> ~/pick_ledgers/facts_random.
scoring: tools/pick_ledger.py rules unchanged: entry at the next open, ratio lift vs SPY, 30 random control names per pick, rank among them, beta-adjusted excess, t clustered by entry month.
verdict: ONE read, on the first 30 picks of the facts ledger, when all 30 have a closed 21-session window (10 weeks of picks plus a month). PASS = mean and median vs SPY > 0, more than half ahead of SPY, mean vs 30 random names > 0, mean rank above the 50th percentile, beta-adjusted > 0, t >= 2.5 with the t clustered by entry WEEK (10 clusters; pick_ledger's month clustering needs four entry months and 30 picks span three), AND a mean vs SPY above the WHOLE-SHEET control: every name on each week's sheet bought at the same open and held 21 sessions, names averaged inside a week, weeks averaged. Anything else = FAIL. Honest size of the evidence: the ten 21-session windows overlap, so 30 picks are about three independent months; the bar is 2.5 instead of 2.0 for that reason, and a PASS is a reason to keep the record running and to size nothing on it yet, not proof. The 63-session figures, the AVOID ledger and the 3-name RANDOM ledger are reported, not judged.
replay: tools/fact_picker.py replay: the same twelve past Mondays as the auto_picker replay (2026-07-27 to 2026-10-12), sheets rebuilt as of each Monday (prices through the prior close, SEC facts by filing date), scored at 21 sessions. A SCREEN ONLY: the agents may have been trained on this period, adjusted prices carry later splits and dividends, and these twelve weeks were already looked at for the headline picker. A good replay does not change the live rule or shorten the live wait; a bad one does not stop the live run. Two more reasons it is only a screen: the stock list was frozen on 2026-10-15 liquidity, after all twelve Mondays, so names that fell out are missing and every replay line is flattered against SPY (compare with the whole-sheet line, not with zero); and it is labelled SCREEN POSITIVE / SCREEN NEGATIVE, never a sign of skill.
end: picks recorded after 2027-11-11 do not count (the ledger's own end date). No change to the prompt wording, the sheet or the combine rule while the live record runs; a change is a new test with a new ledger.
amended: 2026-11-11 late evening ET, after the result-skeptic review (NOT READY: 1 blocker, 5 should-fix) and still before any run on any week. Every finding is applied below and in the code.
operating_rules: A week counts once: if a run fails (an agent does not answer, the sheet cannot be built), it may be rerun later the same week with the same saved sheet and replies; each ledger is filled at most once a week. The agents' models come from the desk config and are stored on every pick; if a model changes inside the first 30 picks the report says so and the read still happens once. The sheet, both replies and the scores are committed to the facts ledger's git record each week. If fewer than 30 picks are recorded by 2027-11-11, or the picker is switched off before the read, the result is UNPROVEN, not a pass. Hands-off catch-up (operator 11/11 'run automatically without intervention', added before any run): the weekday 16:40 nightly job also calls `run`, which does nothing when the week is already recorded; a week first recorded by the nightly job enters at the next open like any other.
known_limits: Multi-class companies use the diluted weighted-average share count, which normally covers all classes; this was not checked name by name. Banks and other filers without a Liabilities tag show n/a for that figure. A company that reports only single quarters (no year-to-date figures) gets no sheet in mid-year.
